narrative: OMX30 opens with conflicting signals: European bourses gain modest ground while US equities crater, particularly tech (NASDAQ -0.78%). The index sits 4.8% above its 200-day MA in an official bull regime, but ADX 42.5 with bearish directional bias and RSI 36.89 suggest downtrend momentum dominates despite the longer-term bullish positioning. MACD below signal with histogram -9.538 and the index trading 0.2% below the 50-MA warn of near-term weakness. Commodity divergence—gold and copper surge while oil retreats—creates sector-level dispersion. USD/SEK +0.29% aids exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson), but NASDAQ weakness dampens sentiment for tech names. Watch for mean reversion given neutral RSI territory and Bollinger positioning in lower half.
morningBrief: OMX30 faces a mixed open: European strength (+0.15% to +0.43%) offsets transatlantic tech selloff (NASDAQ -0.78%). ADX 42.5 bearish DI bias and MACD crossover below signal warn of underlying weakness despite bull regime backdrop. RSI 36.89 neutral but approaching oversold—watch for 3085 support (lower Bollinger band) and 3180 resistance (50-MA). Exporters (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A, Ericsson B) supported by USD/SEK +0.29%, but sentiment remains tepid post-NASDAQ decline. Boliden and mining names catch tailwind from copper +1.92%, gold +1.21%. Banks see mixed signals: 4.996% US 10Y yield aids NIM but VIX -1.34% suggests risk appetite stabilizing—hold on squeeze. Key event: US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET; trade headlines remain binary risk to risk assets.
